applies_why: The judge text uses a tension between a footed covenant-origin analogy and the sentence’s own stated source to mark the verse UNDERDETERMINED, which the rule governs as a two-sense/not-open issue.
quote: D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- the challenger's covenant-origin analogy is footed (1 Chronicles 28:6, Acts 1:8) but the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb; answered in [CR3] LINK 2.
rule_words: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: phrase 'carries two senses at once': (1) the footed covenant-origin analogy and the sentence's own stated source are two senses, so the verse is not open; (2) the analogy is external and the verse states only one sense, so the clause does not apply.
why: By declaring UNDERDETERMINED while acknowledging both a footed covenant-origin analogy and the sentence’s own source statement, the judge treats the two senses as open even though K-S2 says both senses stand and the verse is not open.
